definitions.explanation: In grammar, the part of a sentence that tells what the subject does or is; contains the verb and its complements.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦では→では：02945_deha⟧{述語|じゅつご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{文|ぶん}→文：03716_bun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese, the predicate comes at the end of the sentence.
What is the predicate of this sentence?

examples.japanese: {述語|じゅつご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧⟦だけでなく→〜だけでなく：18373_dakedenaku⟧、⟦{形容詞|けいようし}→形容詞：10419_keiyoushi⟧⟦や→や：10080_ya⟧⟦{名詞|めいし}→名詞：10420_meishi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Not only verbs but also adjectives and nouns can be used as predicates.

notes:
{述語|じゅつご} is a grammatical term used to describe the predicate of a sentence. In Japanese grammar, the predicate typically comes at the end of the sentence.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{主語|しゅご}→主語：00377_shugo⟧: subject
- ⟦{目的語|もくてきご}→目的語：20479_mokutekigo⟧: object
- ⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧: modifier
- ⟦{補語|ほご}→補語：22867_hogo⟧: complement

In Japanese linguistics, predicates can be verbal (⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧), adjectival (⟦{形容詞|けいようし}→形容詞：10419_keiyoushi⟧), or nominal (⟦{名詞|めいし}→名詞：10420_meishi⟧ + だ/⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧).
